**Protocol (identical for every column).** Frozen task seed 7. Uniform budget: the first 20 minutes of each session. Score: the best *harness-verified* value per session — the harness, not the agent, runs the frozen scorer and decides keep/revert. **Baseline** = pristine bundle. **RSI OFF** = shipped engine with the self-improvement loop disabled (`--improver noop`). **RSI ON** = shipped engine with its naive self-editing loop enabled. **Claude** = Claude Code driving the same single editable file under the same keep/revert discipline, 3 independent 20-minute sessions (mean ± SD over the completed sessions).

**Reading the table.** Claude Code, the strongest reference, leads on all five tasks (e.g. 0.7666 vs 0.599 on Colonel Blotto; 9,507 vs 11,552 RMSE on House Price). The two shipped RSI arms are indistinguishable: the ON/OFF gap is at most ~2%, the arms tie on two tasks, and on the other three the naive self-editing loop is nominally *behind* the no-edit control (self-edits are reverted or neutral). That flat ON/OFF contrast is the assignment — the machinery is real, the strategy is not yet.

Generated by the course staff from the raw session logs (RSI training matrices and Claude Code baseline runs). Use it as the fixed comparison protocol when you report your own five-task results.
